_comment: PSF calculator for the emtk window: the parameter panels of psf_calculator.view.json (the AutoForm spec the Qt tool rendered) with spin arrows, drawn by emtk.view_form over PSFPanel (gui/panel.py). The 3-D volume and the slice are drawn by gui/app.py (plots).

sections.description: Export the computed volume, open the guided tour or the help.

buttons.label: Export .npy
buttons.description: Save the computed volume as a NumPy array at full float precision, without metadata. Greyed until a volume exists.

buttons.label: Export .tif
buttons.description: Save the computed volume as a 32-bit ImageJ TIFF stack that carries the voxel size, so ImageJ scales it correctly. Greyed until a volume exists.

buttons.label: Guide
buttons.description: A step-by-step walk through the tool.

buttons.label: Help
buttons.description: Explain the optical models, the polarization and how to read the volume.

sections.title: Objective
sections.description: The objective: numerical aperture, immersion index and the wavelength.

sections.label: NA
sections.description: Numerical aperture. Above about 1.0 the scalar models stop being trustworthy and the vectorial one should be used.

sections.label: n (immersion)
sections.description: Refractive index of the immersion medium: 1.518 oil, 1.33 water, 1.0 air. The NA cannot exceed it.

sections.label: λ (nm)
sections.description: Emission or excitation wavelength in nanometres.

sections.title: Model
sections.description: The optical model that computes the focus.

sections.label: Optical model
sections.description: Vectorial accounts for the longitudinal field and the input polarization; Airy is the exact scalar focal-plane result and is repeated unchanged along z, so it shows no defocus; Gaussian adds a paraxial axial envelope but has no wings.

sections.title: Polarization
sections.description: The polarization of the light at the objective pupil (the vectorial model only; the angle only for linear polarization at an angle).

sections.label: Polarization
sections.description: State of the light entering the pupil. Linear elongates the focus along its own axis; radial has a strong longitudinal core (tighter than linear only with an annular aperture); azimuthal is a doughnut with a zero on axis.

sections.label: Angle (°)
sections.description: Orientation of the linear state, measured from the x axis. Used only when Polarization is 'Linear at angle'.

sections.title: Sampling
sections.description: The grid the volume is computed on, and how finely the aperture integral is evaluated.

sections.label: Lateral size (px)
sections.description: Pixels per lateral side of the volume.

sections.label: Planes
sections.description: Number of axial planes, centred on focus.

sections.label: Pixel (nm)
sections.description: Lateral sampling in nanometres.

sections.label: z step (nm)
sections.description: Axial spacing between planes.

sections.label: Quality
sections.description: Preview uses a coarser aperture quadrature. The vectorial model is expensive, so live editing stays on preview and the full calculation is worth waiting for only once the parameters are settled.

sections.title: Display
sections.description: How the volume is drawn; none of these recompute it.

sections.label: Threshold
sections.description: Hide voxels below this fraction of the peak. A diffraction-limited focus is mostly empty space and renders as fog without it.

sections.label: Gamma
sections.description: Shapes the opacity ramp. Below 1 lifts the faint wings into view.

sections.label: Colormap
sections.description: Colormap of the rendered volume.

sections.label: Polarization vectors
sections.description: Draw the pupil polarization state as strokes on a ring above the focus. Vectorial model only, since the scalar models ignore polarization.
The size of the volume, the lateral and axial FWHM measured on it, and the scalar 0.51 lambda/NA prediction.

sections.label: Slice plane
sections.description: The central section of the volume to show: XY lateral, XZ or YZ axial.
